title: 4v4 Shell Drill
description: The foundational team-defense drill: 4-on-4 in the half court with the ball rotating around the perimeter while defenders practice help, closeouts, and rotations.
goal: Install team defensive principles — help positioning, closeout discipline, and rotation timing — in a controlled 4-on-4 setting.
setup: Four offensive players spaced around the perimeter (two wings, two slots); four defenders matched up.
Start in the half court with the ball on one wing.
A coach stands at the top to call out rotations and freeze the drill for teaching moments.

instructions.title: Ball swings, defense shifts
instructions.detail: Offense passes the ball around the perimeter — no dribbling at first; defenders shift between on-ball, deny, and help positions on every pass.

instructions.title: Add closeouts
instructions.detail: Each pass triggers a closeout from the new on-ball defender while off-ball defenders adjust their help angles.

instructions.title: Add one dribble
instructions.detail: Offense is allowed one dribble per catch to attack closeouts — defenders practice containing the drive and rotating on help.

instructions.title: Go live
instructions.detail: Play 4-on-4 live until the offense scores, the defense gets a stop, or 30 seconds pass; reset and go again.

instructions.title: Score the defense
instructions.detail: Defense earns a point for every stop; offense earns a point per basket. First to 7 wins the round.

coachingPoints: See ball and man — defenders should be in stance with vision split between their matchup and the ball.
Help defenders: one step off the line between your man and the ball, ready to stunt or rotate.
Close out under control — the shell exposes every lazy closeout instantly.
Talk constantly: 'ball!', 'help left!', 'shooter!' — silent shell is broken shell.
commonMistakes: Ball-watching and losing your man on cuts — keep your head on a swivel.
Help defenders standing straight up — help position is a low stance, not a resting spot.
progression: Add a fifth player both sides (5-on-5 shell), allow unlimited dribbles, or add ball screens to force pick-and-roll coverage decisions.
regression: Walk through rotations without live offense, reduce to 3-on-3, or keep the no-dribble rule for the whole drill.
gameApplication: Shell drill is where team defense is built — every rotation, closeout, and help decision in a game traces back to these reps.
